record.statement:
In the Gaussian white-noise sequence model defined on page 35, let $0<\beta_1<\beta_2$ and $0<M_1<M_2<\infty$ be fixed, and let $D$ be arbitrary. For $\beta\in[\beta_1,\beta_2]$ and $M\in[M_1,M_2]$, define $\rho_{n,\beta,M}$ by
\[
\rho_{n,\beta,M}^{(4\beta+1)/(4\beta)}=n^{-1}M^{1/(4\beta)}\eta_\beta^{-1}\bigl((2\log\log n)^{1/2}+D\bigr).
\]
Does there exist a sequence of tests $(\phi_n)$, not depending on the unknown $(\beta,M)$ and satisfying $E_{n,0}\phi_n\le \alpha+o(1)$, such that
\[
\sup_{\beta\in[\beta_1,\beta_2],\,M\in[M_1,M_2]}
\Psi_n\bigl(\phi_n,\rho_{n,\beta,M},\beta,M\bigr)
\le (1-\alpha)\Phi(-D)+o(1)?
\]
The report answers yes in Theorem 3.

record.title: Quantitative Faber–Krahn inequality with Fraenkel asymmetry
record.statement:
For a fixed dimension $N$, there exists a constant $\c3=\c3(N)>0$ such that every open set $\a9\subset\mathbb{R}^N$ with finite measure satisfies

$$|\a9|^{2/N}\bbda(\a9)-|B|^{2/N}\bbda(B)\geq\c3\,\cal{A}(\a9)^2,$$

where $\bbda(\a9)$ is the first Dirichlet eigenvalue of $\minus\Delta$ on $\a9$, $B$ is an $N$-dimensional ball with $|B|=|\a9|$, and

$$\cal{A}(\a9)=\inf\left\{\frac{|\a9\triangle\ B|}{|B|}: B\text{ is a ball with }|B|=|\a9|\right\}.$$

The report labels this assertion as a conjecture on page 25 and gives a theorem on page 26 asserting that it holds for every such open set.

record.title: Quantum Gaussian optimizers for gauge-covariant and contravariant channels
record.statement:
Let \(\Phi\) be a gauge-covariant or gauge-contravariant Bosonic Gaussian channel, as defined by equations (2)–(5) on PDF pages 29–30, and let \(f:[0,1]\to\mathbb{R}\) be concave with \(f(0)=0\). Then
\[
\operatorname{Tr} f(\Phi[\rho])\geq \operatorname{Tr}f\bigl(\Phi[|w\rangle\langle w|]\bigr)=\operatorname{Tr}f\bigl(\Phi[|0\rangle\langle0|]\bigr)
\]
for every state \(\rho\) and every coherent state \(|w\rangle\langle w|\). If, in addition, \(f\) is strictly concave, \(KK^*>0\), and the relevant inequalities (3) and (5) hold strictly, equality occurs only when \(\rho\) is a coherent state.

record.title: Spectral-measure parametrization for a canonical system
record.statement:
Consider the canonical system $-Jy'(x)=zH(x)y(x)$ on $[0,\ell)$ with $y_2(0)=0$, where $H$ is a real symmetric non-negative measurable $2\times2$ matrix, $\operatorname{tr}H(x)=1$ almost everywhere, and $\int_0^\varepsilon h_{22}(x)\,dx>0$ for every $\varepsilon>0$. Let $W(x;z)=(w_{ij}(x;z))_{i,j=1}^2$ solve $\frac{dW(x;z)}{dx}J=zW(x;z)H(x)$, $W(0;z)=I_2$. If $0<b\leq\ell$, $b<\infty$, and $\gamma\in\widetilde{N}:=N\cup\{\infty\}$, then
$$m_\gamma(z):=\frac{w_{11}(b;z)\gamma(z)+w_{12}(b;z)}{w_{21}(b;z)\gamma(z)+w_{22}(b;z)}$$
belongs to the class $N$ and has the representation
$$m_\gamma(z)=\alpha+\int_{-\infty}^{\infty}\left(\frac{1}{\lambda-z}-\frac{\lambda}{1+\lambda^2}\right)d\tau_\gamma(\lambda),\qquad z\in\mathbb{C}\setminus\mathbb{R},$$
for some $\alpha\in\mathbb{R}$.

record.title: Agol–Leininger–Margalit bounds for pseudo-Anosov stretch factors and homology
record.statement:
Let $S_g$ be a closed orientable surface of genus $g\ge 2$. For a pseudo-Anosov homeomorphism $f:S_g\to S_g$, let $\kappa(f)=\dim\operatorname{Fix}(f_*)$, where $f_*$ is the induced action on $H_1(S_g;\mathbb R)$. Define
\[
\ell_g(k)=\min\{\log(\lambda(f))\mid f:S_g\to S_g\text{ is pseudo-Anosov and }\kappa(f)\ge k\}.
\]
Then, for all $g\ge 2$ and $0\le k\le 2g$,
\[
0.00031\,\frac{k+1}{2g-2}\le \ell_g(k)\le 12\log(2)\,\frac{k+1}{2g-2}.
\]
Equivalently, $\ell_g(k)\asymp (k+1)/g$.

record.title: Absolute linear Harbourne constants for at most ten lines
record.statement:
Let $K$ be an arbitrary field, and let $\mathcal L=\{L_1,\ldots,L_d\}$ be a configuration of $d$ mutually distinct lines in $\mathbb P^2(K)$. If $\mathcal P(\mathcal L)=\{P_1,\ldots,P_s\}$ is the set of singular points and $m_{\mathcal L}(P_k)$ is the number of lines through $P_k$, define
\[
H_L(K,\mathcal L)=\frac{d^2-\sum_{k=1}^s m_{\mathcal L}(P_k)^2}{s},\qquad H_L(K,d)=\min_{\mathcal L}H_L(K,\mathcal L),
\]
and
\[
H_L(d)=\min_K H_L(K,d).
\]
The absolute linear Harbourne constants for $2\le d\le 10$ are
\[
\begin{array}{c|ccccccccc}
d&2&3&4&5&6&7&8&9&10\\ \hline
H_L(d)&0&-1&-\frac43&-\frac32&-\frac{12}{7}&-2&-2&-\frac94&-\frac{29}{12}
\end{array}
\]

record.statement: For a prime $p$, let $n_p(\varepsilon)$ be the least positive integer such that, for every $n\ge n_p(\varepsilon)$ and every subset $A\subseteq\mathbb{F}_p^n$ of density $\alpha$, there is a nonzero $d\in\mathbb{F}_p^n$ such that the density of three-term arithmetic progressions with common difference $d$ that are in $A$ is at least $\alpha^3-\varepsilon$. record.title: Turán inequality for partially directed uniform hypergraphs
record.statement:
**Conjecture 4.** Fix $k\ge 2$. For all sufficiently large $n$ (depending on $k$), every $n$-vertex partially directed $k$-uniform hypergraph ($k$-PDG) without $\vec T_k$ as a subgraph satisfies
\[
\alpha+(\log_2 3)\beta\le 1,
\]
where $\alpha$ is the number of undirected edges divided by $\binom{n}{k}$ and $\beta$ is the number of directed edges divided by $\binom{n}{k}$. Here a $k$-PDG is obtained by orienting some edges of a $k$-uniform hypergraph, with an oriented edge recording a selected vertex; subgraphs may be formed by deleting vertices, edges, and orientations. The forbidden $k$-PDG $\vec T_k$ is obtained from $\vec T_2$, whose edges are $12$, the directed edge $1\to 3$, and $23$, by adding $k-2$ common vertices to all three edges.

record.title: Hadamard conjecture
record.statement:
For a positive integer $n$, call a matrix $H$ a *Hadamard matrix of order $n$*
if

$$
H\in\{-1,1\}^{n\times n},\qquad HH^{\mathsf{T}}=n\,I_{n},
$$

where $I_{n}$ is the $n\times n$ identity matrix and $H^{\mathsf{T}}$ is the
transpose of $H$; equivalently, the rows of $H$ are pairwise orthogonal vectors
in $\mathbb{R}^{n}$, so that any two distinct rows of $H$ agree in exactly
$n/2$ of the $n$ coordinates, and $|\det H|=n^{n/2}$.

For every positive integer $k$ there exists a Hadamard matrix of order $4k$.

record.statement:
For a positive integer $n$, call a matrix $M=(m_{i,j})_{i,j=0}^{n-1}$ with
entries $m_{i,j}\in\{+1,-1\}$ circulant if $m_{i,j}$ depends only on
$j-i \bmod n$, i.e. there is a sequence
$(a_0,a_1,\dots,a_{n-1})\in\{+1,-1\}^n$ with $m_{i,j}=a_{(j-i)\bmod
n}$ for all $i,j$, and symmetric if $M^{\mathsf T}=M$. Four matrices
$A,B,C,D$ of order $n$ are Williamson matrices of order
$n$ if each of them has all entries in $\{+1,-1\}$, each is symmetric and
circulant, and

$$
A^{2}+B^{2}+C^{2}+D^{2}=4n\,I_{n},
$$

where $I_{n}$ is the identity matrix of order $n$.

For every positive integer $n$, there exist Williamson matrices of order $n$.

record.title: Köthe conjecture
record.statement:
Let
$R$ be an associative ring, not necessarily commutative and not necessarily possessing a multiplicative identity. An element $a
\in R$ is nilpotent if $a^{n} = 0$ for some integer $n \ge
1$, and a subset of $R$ is called nil if each of its elements is nilpotent.
Then:

If the only nil two-sided ideal of $R$ is $\{0\}$, then the only nil one-sided
(left or right) ideal of $R$ is $\{0\}$.

Equivalently, for every associative ring $R$ and all nil left ideals $I, J
\subseteq R$, the left ideal $I + J$ is nil.

record.title: Lebesgue's universal covering problem
record.statement:
For a nonempty set $S \subset \mathbb{R}^2$ let

$$
\operatorname{diam}(S) = \sup\{\, |x-y| : x, y \in S \,\},
$$

where $|\cdot|$ denotes the Euclidean norm. Say that a set $C \subset
\mathbb{R}^2$ *covers* $S$ if there is an isometry
$\varphi$ of the plane (translations, rotations and reflections being allowed) with $\varphi(S)
\subseteq C$. Call a compact convex set $C \subset
\mathbb{R}^2$ a *universal cover* if $C$ covers every set
$S \subset \mathbb{R}^2$ with $\operatorname{diam}(S) \le 1$, and put

$$
\alpha = \inf \{\, \operatorname{area}(C) : C \subset \mathbb{R}^2 \text{ a compact convex universal cover} \,\}.
$$

Determine the exact value of
$\alpha$, and exhibit a compact convex universal cover $C$ with
$\operatorname{area}(C) = \alpha$.

record.title: Hadwiger–Nelson problem
record.statement:
For a set $S$, call a map $c:\mathbb{R}^{2}\to S$ a proper coloring of the plane
if

$$
c(x)\neq c(y)\quad\text{whenever } x,y\in\mathbb{R}^{2} \text{ satisfy } |x-y|=1,
$$

where $|\cdot|$ denotes the Euclidean norm. Equivalently, let $G$ be the
unit-distance graph of the plane: the graph whose vertex set is
$\mathbb{R}^{2}$, with $xy$ an edge if and only if
$|x-y|=1$; a proper coloring of the plane is exactly a proper vertex coloring of $G$.

Determine the chromatic number of the plane,

$$
\chi(G)=\min\bigl\{\,k\in\mathbb{N} \;:\; \text{there exists a proper coloring } c:\mathbb{R}^{2}\to\{1,\dots,k\}\,\bigr\},
$$

that is, the least number of colors with which the points of the plane can be
colored so that no two points at distance exactly $1$ receive the same color.

$M$ be a topological manifold (a Hausdorff space, locally homeomorphic to $\mathbb{R}^{n}$
for some $n \ge 0$), and let
$G$ be a locally compact topological group. Say that a continuous action $\Phi
\colon G \times M \to M$, written $\Phi(g,x) = g \cdot
x$, is *effective* (faithful) if its kernel is trivial, i.e. if $g \in
G$ satisfies $g \cdot x = x$ for every $x \in M$, then $g$ is the identity
element of $G$.

For every locally compact topological group
$G$ admitting a continuous effective action on a topological manifold $M$, the
group $G$ is a Lie group, i.e. $G$ carries a smooth manifold structure
compatible with its topology for which multiplication and inversion are smooth.

Equivalently: for every prime number $p$, the additive group $\mathbb{Z}_{p}$ of
$p$-adic integers, with its usual compact topology, admits no continuous
effective action on any topological manifold.

record.title: Kadison–Singer problem
record.statement:
Let
$\ell^2$ denote the Hilbert space of square-summable sequences of complex numbers, with standard orthonormal basis $(e_n)_{n\in\mathbb{N}}$.
Let
$B$ be the C*-algebra of all bounded (continuous) linear operators from $\ell^2$
to $\ell^2$, and let $D\subseteq
B$ be the C*-subalgebra consisting of those operators that are diagonal with respect to $(e_n)_{n\in\mathbb{N}}$,
i.e. of those $T\in B$ for which there is a bounded sequence
$(\lambda_n)_{n\in\mathbb{N}}$ of complex numbers with $Te_n=\lambda_n
e_n$ for all $n$. Both $B$ and $D$ contain the identity operator $I$.

For a C*-algebra $A$ with multiplicative identity $I$, a *state* on
$A$ is a continuous linear functional $\varphi:A\to\mathbb{C}$ such that
$\varphi(I)=1$ and $\varphi(T)\geq 0$ for every positive $T\in
A$ (i.e. every $T$ of the form $T=S^*S$). The set of states on $A$ is convex,
and a state
$\varphi$ is called *pure* if it is an extreme point of this set, that is, if $\varphi=t\varphi_1+(1-t)\varphi_2$
with $0<t<1$ and $\varphi_1,\varphi_2$ states on
$A$ forces $\varphi_1=\varphi_2=\varphi$. A state $\psi$ on $B$ is said to
*extend* a state $\varphi$ on $D$ if $\psi(T)=\varphi(T)$ for all $T\in D$.

For every pure state $\varphi$ on $D$ there exists exactly one state
$\psi$ on $B$ that extends $\varphi$.

record.title: Conjecture on the limiting degree distribution of random planar graphs
record.statement:
For each integer $k\geq 1$, let $Z^{(k)}_n$ denote the proportion of vertices of degree $k$ in a uniformly random planar graph with $n$ vertices. **Limiting degree-distribution conjecture.** As $n\to\infty$, the random variable $Z^{(k)}_n$ converges in law to an explicit constant $\pi^{(k)}$, and these constants satisfy

$$
\sum_k\pi^{(k)}=1.
$$

This conjecture proposes a limiting probability distribution for vertex degrees in uniformly random planar graphs; the stated passage does not indicate that it has been resolved.

record.title: Hinkkanen–Martin conjecture on Julia sets of polynomial semigroups
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a polynomial semigroup, and write $J(G)$ for its Julia set. Suppose that there is an element $h\in G$ such that $J_h=J(G)$, and assume that $J(G)$ is not a line segment.

**Hinkkanen–Martin's modified conjecture.** For all $f,g\in G$, one has

$$
J_f=J_g.
$$

Consequently, $G$ is nearly abelian.

The original statement without the condition that $J(G)$ is not a line segment is refuted by a counterexample in the paper, whose Julia set is a closed line segment. The modified statement is explicitly described as unresolved.

record.title: Spectral bounded isometry conjecture
record.statement:
Let $(M,\omega)$ be a symplectic manifold, let $\operatorname{Symp}_0(M,\omega)$ be its identity component, and let $\operatorname{Ham}(M,\omega)$ be the Hamiltonian subgroup. Let $\operatorname{BI}_0(M,\omega,\gamma)$ denote the subgroup of symplectomorphisms bounded with respect to the spectral norm $\gamma$. **Spectral bounded isometry conjecture.**

$$
\operatorname{BI}_0(M,\omega,\gamma)=\operatorname{Ham}(M,\omega)\qquad\text{for all }(M,\omega).
$$

This is the spectral-norm analogue of the bounded isometry conjecture for the Hofer norm. The source formulates it as a conjecture after noting that the Hofer version is very hard and that partial results are known.

record.title: The jumping-sequence characterization of the infinite admissible set
record.statement:
Let $w(i,j)=j/i$ be the weight function, and let $\mathcal{A}_\infty=\{1,3,8,22,60,\ldots\}$. Let $d(0)=1$ and, for $n\geq 1$, define

$$
d(n)=\lfloor e d(n-1)+0.5\rfloor.
$$

Thus the sequence begins $1,3,8,22,60,163,443,\ldots$.

**Jumping-sequence characterization.** The set $\mathcal{A}_\infty$ is composed of the elements of the integer sequence $d(n)$.

The preceding results show that the sequence elements can belong to $\mathcal{A}_\infty$ and provide an upper bound excluding sufficiently large integers outside the sequence, but the paper notes that the available rounding estimates do not establish this characterization.

record.title: Chan–Leung's facet-point conjecture for reflexive polytopes
record.statement:
Let $P$ be a reflexive polytope with barycenter $b_P=0$. For a facet $F$ of $P$, let a facet $G$ be adjacent to $F$ when there is a vector $u_G$ such that

$$
\langle u_G,G\rangle=-1,\qquad \langle u_G,P\rangle\geq -1.
$$

**Chan–Leung's facet-point conjecture.** If $b_P=0$, then for every facet $F$ there exists a point $x_F\in\operatorname{aff}(F)$ such that

$$
\langle u_G,x_F\rangle\leq\frac12
$$

for every facet $G$ of $P$ adjacent to $F$.

The conjecture was proposed as a combinatorial ingredient for proving the Chan–Leung Chern-number inequality without additional assumptions. The source gives a five-dimensional counterexample, so the assertion is refuted.

record.title: Hilbert-scheme identity for character varieties
record.statement:
Let $\mathcal H_\lambda(z,w)$ be the partition function appearing in the source, let $\phi(0):=0$, and for every nonzero partition $\lambda$ define

$$
\phi_\lambda(z,w):=\sum_{(i,j)\in\lambda}z^{j-1}w^{i-1},
$$

where the sum is over the boxes of $\lambda$. **Hilbert-scheme identity.** The following formal power-series identity is conjectured:

$$
1+(z^2-1)(1-w^2)\frac{\sum_\lambda\mathcal H_\lambda(z,w)\phi_\lambda(z^2,w^2)T^{|\lambda|}}{\sum_\lambda\mathcal H_\lambda(z,w)T^{|\lambda|}}=\prod_{n\geq1}\frac{(1-zwT^n)^2}{(1-z^2T^n)(1-w^2T^n)}.
$$

It arises by combining the Hilbert-scheme formula with the main conjecture in the case $g=1$ and $\mu=(n-1,1)$, giving a purely combinatorial reformulation.

record.title: Capacity sparsity conjecture for transient random-walk aggregation
record.statement:
Let $R$ be a transient random walk on $\mathbb{Z}$, and let $A_n$ be the aggregate after $n$ particles. Write $\operatorname{Cap}(A_n)$ for its capacity. **Capacity sparsity conjecture.** Almost surely,

$$
\operatorname{Cap}(A_n)=o(n).
$$

record.title: The projector relation for braided trace powers
record.statement:
Let ${\rm Tr}_R L^k\in {\cal L}^k(R)$ be the braided trace power, and let $P_+^{(k)}$ and $P_{+2}^{(k-1)}$ be the symmetrizer operators acting on the corresponding tensor powers. **Projector relation.** For every positive integer $k$ for which these operators are defined, the relation

$$
P_+^{(k)}{\rm Tr}_R L^k=P_{+2}^{(k-1)}{\rm Tr}_R L^k
$$

holds. This identity is used to put the homogeneous element ${\rm Tr}_R L^k$ into the canonical form required before applying the differential in the complex of braided differential forms. The source presents the relation without resolving its general status; the preceding discussion indicates that explicit projector constructions are known only in low degrees.

record.statement:
Let $\mathcal{A}$ be a simple arrangement of $n$ hyperplanes in dimension $d$, and let $H_\mathcal{A}(n,d)$ be the maximum average graph diameter of its bounded cells.

**Hyperplane Diameter Conjecture.**

$$
H_\mathcal{A}(n,d) \leq d.
$$

The conjecture concerns the average diameter of bounded cells in simple hyperplane arrangements. The supplied material gives no resolution status.
